title: Email & calendar
blurb: Outlook, Apple Mail and webmail: not sending, not syncing, password prompts, calendar trouble.

remedies.title: Set up or fix my email signature
remedies.why: Signatures are saved per app and device; the new Outlook and Outlook on the web keep theirs online.

steps.text: Outlook: Settings (gear) › Mail › Signatures (new Outlook / web); classic: File › Options › Mail › Signatures.
Apple Mail: Mail › Settings › Signatures.
Pick it as default for new messages and replies.
Logos sent as attachments often show as files; use small hosted images or none.

remedies.escalate: Some workplaces add signatures centrally; IT manages those.

remedies.title: Outlook data file is too large or damaged
symptoms: outlook data file reached maximum size
remedies.why: Classic Outlook keeps mail in .ost/.pst files that can grow huge or get damaged.

steps.text: For a work account (.ost), close Outlook and delete or rename the .ost in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Outlook; Outlook downloads it again.
For a .pst, run the Inbox Repair Tool (SCANPST.EXE in the Office install folder) on a copy first.
Archive old mail or move it to the online archive to keep the file smaller.

remedies.escalate: Back up any .pst before repairs; IT can help import it into your mailbox.

remedies.title: Outlook suggests an old or wrong email address
remedies.why: Outlook remembers addresses you typed before, including old ones.

steps.text: Start typing the name, highlight the wrong suggestion and click its X (or press Delete).
Classic Outlook: File › Options › Mail › Empty Auto-Complete List clears all.

remedies.title: Email rules don't run
remedies.why: Some rules only run while Outlook on this computer is open (client-only), or a rule above stops later ones.

steps.text: Make rules in Outlook on the web; those run on the server even when your computer is off.
Check rule order and "stop processing more rules" ticks.
Mailboxes have a size limit for rules; delete old ones.

remedies.title: I sent an email by mistake: can I recall it?
remedies.why: Recall only works inside the same organisation and before it's read; undo-send gives a few seconds to cancel.

steps.text: Outlook: open the sent message › ⋯ › Recall message (works best inside your organisation).
Turn on Undo send for next time: Outlook › Settings › Mail › Compose and reply; Gmail › Settings › Undo Send.
If it held sensitive data sent outside, tell IT/your manager rather than relying on recall.

remedies.escalate: Personal or confidential data sent to the wrong person is a data incident; report it.

remedies.title: Share my calendar or open someone else's
remedies.why: Calendars are shared with permissions from Outlook or the web.

steps.text: Share: Outlook calendar › Share › add the person › choose what they can see or edit.
Open someone's: Calendar › Add calendar › From directory (or open the invitation they sent).
Apple Calendar shares iCloud calendars: right-click the calendar › Share Calendar.

remedies.title: People don't get my meeting invitations (or I don't get theirs)
remedies.why: Invitations are emails; junk filters, rules, or a delegate handling invites can catch them.

steps.text: Check Junk and any rule that moves mail.
Check Outlook's delegate settings: if someone manages your calendar, invites may go to them.
Resend as a fresh invite; send outside guests a link too.

remedies.title: Add Gmail, iCloud or Yahoo mail to Outlook or Apple Mail
remedies.why: These services want modern sign-in or an app-specific password, not your normal password.

steps.text: Add the account and let it open the provider's sign-in page; approve it there.
If it asks for a password and refuses yours, create an app password in the provider's account security settings (iCloud, Yahoo; Gmail with 2-step).
Add accounts to Apple Mail through Internet Accounts.

remedies.title: Email bounced back ("undeliverable" / "delivery failed")
remedies.why: The address is wrong, the other mailbox is full, or the other side rejected your mail.

steps.text: Read the code in the bounce: 550/5.1.1 usually means the address doesn't exist; check the spelling.
"Mailbox full": the recipient must clear space; try later.
Rejected as spam/policy: send without large attachments or links, or contact them another way.

remedies.escalate: Forward the bounce to IT if many messages to different people bounce.

remedies.title: Outlook changed to the "new Outlook" (or I want to switch)
remedies.why: Microsoft is moving people to the new Outlook; some features (PST files, some add-ins) work differently.

steps.text: Switch with the "New Outlook" toggle at the top right of Outlook.
In the new Outlook, Settings › General › About Outlook offers going back to classic while it's allowed.

remedies.escalate: Your organisation may control which Outlook you get.
